milestone: Iterator27: owning copied detached yield-from returns
status: Implemented, validated and independently accepted; pointwise composed over ada32a063/403.
scope: Direct-root ordinary Generator call-unpack after an independently completed child copies an owning object or array return into a simple-CV assigned yield from. The parent has no other owning suspended task or HELD value, no parked history and inactive GC. Real next consumption and forced close are separate paths; active-chain owning unpack and pending APIs remain excluded.
semantics: Child completion copies its return into the parent result slot and detaches the child. Null-key unpack raises the real Error before target entry or argument sending, leaving that continuation available. Normal next transfers its single value owner into RESULT and executes the parent body.

Forced close moves the exact waiting COMPLETE value to request retention before collecting frame jobs, without decrement or duplicate return job. Parent finally and current-cache cleanup remain ordinary. The receipt owns only the value; parent/child indices and source metadata are borrowed, including after allocation retirement.

Retained arrays keep their live embedded reference cells. A later cell write retires the old referent while the new referent stays through the array. A temporary parent cache destructor can replace the unpack Error before caller catch with the original Error as Previous; the distinct copied return remains request-store-late.
source_authority: vendor/php-src/Zend/zend_generators.c::zend_generator_update_current copies a completed child retval into the parent YIELD_FROM result.var while the parent opline remains at YIELD_FROM, then detaches/releases the child.

Zend/zend_compile.c::zend_compile_yield_from uses a temporary result; Zend/zend_opcode.c::emit_live_range starts its default TMPVAR range after that opcode. Zend/zend_execute.c::cleanup_live_vars and zend_generator_cleanup_unfinished_execution explain the unfinished-slot close boundary. The Generator storage destructor preserves ordinary finally/cache cleanup and request-store destructor order.
These are pinned implementation observations, not portable lifetime guarantees. No engine bug or intentional divergence is classified.
